```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Post-CMP Scrub &   │
│      Metrology       │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Objective & Scope

Establish the baseline recipe for void-free Tungsten (W) chemical vapor deposition (CVD) fill and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) over the shared bitline contact (BLC) of the 180nm 1T1C $8F^2$ DRAM cell architecture. The bitline contact is shared between two adjacent access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), providing low-resistance electrical coupling into the folded bitline while maintaining junction leakage below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Clean and Deglaze
1. Transfer wafers into an automated wet bench for pre-metal contact clean.
2. Perform dilute hydrofluoric acid deglaze (`DHF 100:1`, $23^\circ\text{C}$, $45\text{ s}$) to strip native oxide inside high-aspect-ratio contact vias ($CD \approx 180\text{ nm}$) without undercutting inter-layer dielectric (ILD).
3. Follow with standard mega-sonic UPW (ultra-pure water) rinse and surface passivating IPA vapor dry.

#### Step 2: Ti/TiN Adhesion & Diffusion Barrier Deposition
1. Load into multi-chamber cluster tool under high vacuum ($< 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ Torr}$).
2. Perform in-situ Ar plasma pre-sputter etch ($30\text{ s}$, bias RF $100\text{ W}$) to clear contact interfaces at the active area diffusion.
3. Deposit ionized metal plasma (IMP) / ALD Ti liner ($10\text{ nm} \pm 1\text{ nm}$) for contact silicidation and ohmic junction contact.
4. Deposit metal-organic CVD / ALD TiN barrier layer ($15\text{ nm} \pm 1.5\text{ nm}$) using $\text{TDMAT}$ or $\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{NH}_3$ chemistry at $400^\circ\text{C}$ to prevent fluorine attack from subsequent $\text{WF}_6$ precursor chemistry.

#### Step 3: Tungsten Nucleation & Bulk CVD Fill
1. **Silane Reduction Nucleation:** Inject $\text{WF}_6$ ($30\text{ sccm}$) and $\text{SiH}_4$ ($15\text{ sccm}$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$, chamber pressure $30\text{ Torr}$ for $12\text{ s}$ to deposit a thin ($15\text{ nm}$ to $20\text{ nm}$), conformal W nucleation seed layer.
2. **Hydrogen Reduction Bulk Deposition:** Switch chemistry to $\text{WF}_6$ ($150\text{ sccm}$) and $\text{H}_2$ ($2500\text{ sccm}$) at $425^\circ\text{C}$, chamber pressure $80\text{ Torr}$.
3. Target bulk W overburden thickness: $350\text{ nm} \pm 25\text{ nm}$ over ILD field to ensure complete, void-free seam closure inside the $180\text{ nm}$ bitline contact plug.

#### Step 4: Tungsten CMP (Planarization) & Endpoint Detection
1. **Platen 1 (Bulk W Removal):** Apply silica-based acidic oxidizer slurry ($\text{pH } 2.0\text{--}2.5$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ oxidizer), down-force $3.2\text{ psi}$, platen speed $85\text{ rpm}$, carrier speed $80\text{ rpm}$. Polish through bulk W overburden.
2. **Platen 2 (Barrier & Endpoint Clearing):** Switch to high-selectivity barrier polish slurry ($W:\text{TiN}:\text{Oxide} \approx 1:1:0.1$) with optical motor current / eddy-current endpoint detection (EPD) to clear Ti/TiN barrier over ILD with controlled over-polish ($10\%$).
3. **Platen 3 (Buff & Soft Clean):** Soft touch-up buffing on poromeric polyurethane pad with DIW/surfactant to mitigate micro-scratches and particle adherence.

#### Step 5: Post-CMP Cleaning & Defect Inspection
1. Inline double-sided PVA sponge scrub clean using dilute alkaline/surfactant cleaning agent ($0.5\text{ wt}\%\text{ TMAH/NH}_4\text{OH}$, $\text{pH } 10.5$).
2. Spin rinse dry (SRD) with hot $\text{N}_2$ blanket.
3. Conduct in-line metrology (ellipsometry/profilometry for erosion/dishing, brightfield optical defect inspection, and electrical four-point probe contact resistance test).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method & Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Contact Plug Seam / Void Diameter** | $\le 0\text{ nm}$ (Zero voiding / full fill at $180\text{ nm}$ via) | In-line Cross-Section STEM / High-Resolution CD-SEM |
| **W-Plug Dishing & Oxide Erosion** | $\le 15\text{ nm}$ dishing; $\le 10\text{ nm}$ field erosion | Atomic Force Profilometry (AFP) / In-line Optical Profilometer |
| **Bitline Contact Leakage Current** | $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Automated Parametric Wafer Probe (Keithley S530 / Keysight B1500A) |
| **Post-CMP Defectivity (Particles/Residue)** | $\le 20\text{ defects/wafer}$ (size threshold $\ge 0.18\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) | Darkfield/Brightfield Laser Defect Inspection (KLA / Applied Materials) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Defines the unit cell geometry: access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Specifies shared bitline contact between adjacent memory cells in $8F^2$ stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture.
  - Establishes the junction and sub-threshold leakage limit: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to preserve storage retention and meet refresh interval requirements.
  - Confirms the tungsten plug (W-plug) metallization scheme connecting active source/drain regions through the ILD stack.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Chamber Evacuation & Base Vacuum Qualification:**
   - Pump down the cluster PVD deposition chamber via cryopump/turbomolecular pump until the vacuum gauge reads below $2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$ before initiating wafer transfer.
2. **Wafer Pre-Treatment & Degas:**
   - Transfer wafer through loadlock into the degas chamber module. Heat substrate chuck to drive off adsorbed moisture.
   - Perform soft in-situ RF sputter clean / degas to clear native oxide inside the shared bitline contact vias ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$).
3. **Ti Adhesion Layer Sputter Deposition:**
   - Strike DC magnetron plasma with high-purity Argon gas (Ar 99.999%) maintained at an operating pressure of $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$.
   - Apply DC magnetron target power calibrated within $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$ to deposit the primary titanium (Ti) contact silicide precursor and adhesion seed layer.
4. **TiN Barrier Layer Reactive Sputter Deposition:**
   - Introduce ultra-pure reactive Nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) into the Ar sputter ambient.
   - Reactively sputter titanium nitride (TiN) diffusion barrier over the Ti layer at a controlled deposition rate of $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$ to prevent WF₆ chemical attack and tungsten encroachment during downstream W-plug fill.
5. **Post-Deposition Anneal & Barrier Stabilization:**
   - Transfer wafers under vacuum to the thermal anneal station.
   - Run post-deposition forming gas anneal ($\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$) at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$ (or rapid thermal silicidation) to form low-resistance ohmic contacts and densify the barrier microstructure.

| **Ar Working Sputter Pressure** | $3\text{ to }5$ | $\text{mTorr}$ | Capacitance Manometer |
| **DC Magnetron Target Power** | $1.5\text{ to }3.0$ | $\text{kW}$ | Generator Closed-Loop Power Monitor |

| **Post-Anneal Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)** | $< 0.08$ | $\Omega/\Box$ | 4-Point Probe (4PP) Metrology Station |

### 5. Context Literature Citations

- **[Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects]:** Base pressure $< 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$; high-purity Ar ($99.999\%$) working gas pressure $3\text{ to }5\text{ mTorr}$; DC magnetron target power $1.5\text{ to }3.0\text{ kW}$; deposition rate $50\text{ to }100\text{ nm/minute}$; post-metal anneal forming gas $\text{N}_2/\text{H}_2\text{ }95/5$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$; sheet resistance target $R_s < 0.08\ \Omega/\Box$.

- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]:** 1T1C stacked capacitor integration over contact plugs; cell dimensions and thermal process constraints.

## Title: Tungsten (W) CVD Contact Via Fill and Keyhole Void Optimization Recipe
**Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | 8F² Cell Folded Bitline Architecture | Contact Aspect Ratio Fill

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
│    Metrology & CMP     │
│         Polish         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Pre-Clean & Degas**:
   - Transfer wafer into the CVD/PVD cluster degas chamber.
   - Degas wafer under high vacuum at $400^\circ\text{C}$ to desorb moisture, organic residue, and trapped fluorine.
2. **Ti/TiN Liner/Barrier Deposition**:
   - Deposit conformal $\text{Ti}$ adhesion layer followed by $\text{TiN}$ barrier layer via collimated/ionized PVD or CVD to prevent $\text{WF}_6$ wormhole encroachment into the access transistor source/drain diffusion regions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$).
3. **Silane ($\text{SiH}_4$) Reduction Nucleation Step**:
   - Transfer to the W-CVD reaction chamber.
   - Pre-purge with Ar/$\text{N}_2$ carrier gas.
   - Run short silane reduction flash: $\text{WF}_6 + \text{SiH}_4 \rightarrow \text{W} + \text{SiF}_4\uparrow$ at $400^\circ\text{C}$ stage temperature to establish a continuous, thin, fine-grained tungsten seed layer ($\sim 20\text{--}30\,\text{nm}$) on the $\text{TiN}$ surface.
4. **Hydrogen ($\text{H}_2$) Reduction Bulk Fill & Seam Optimization**:
   - Transition gas flows to $\text{H}_2/\text{WF}_6$ reduction chemistry: $\text{WF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{W} + 6\text{HF}\uparrow$.
   - Maintain wafer substrate temperature at $400^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Maintain high $\text{H}_2 : \text{WF}_6$ ratio to achieve bottom-up, conformal, columnar grain growth across the bitline and storage contact vias (aspect ratio $\sim 3:1$ to $4:1$ on the $360\text{--}400\,\text{nm}$ pitch array).
   - Suppress premature mouth closure (pinch-off) at the top rim of the contact to eliminate keyhole/centerline voids.
5. **Overfill & CMP Polish**:
   - Deposit tungsten overburden ($350\,\text{nm} \pm 5\%$ equivalent target clearance above the dielectric field).
   - Send wafer to post-CVD W-CMP to planarize flush to the interlayer dielectric (ILD) surface.

---

  - *Context*: Transistor channel geometry ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), shared bitline contact arrangement, and drain contact tungsten plug (W-plug) connection to the stacked capacitor over bitline (COB).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## W-CMP Planarization Baseline Recipe Setup, Over-Polish Control, and Dishing Metrology

**Context & Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) | Gen 2 (µm)  
**Functional Domain:** Chemical Mechanical Polishing (CMP) / Shared Bitline Contact W-Plug Fill  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 1: Pre-Clean &  │
│  Baseline Inspection  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 2: Main W Bulk  │
│    Polish Platen 1    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 3: Ti/TiN     │
│    Barrier Polish     │
│       Platen 2        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 4: Over-Polish  │
│  & Oxide Stop Platen  │
│           3           │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Step 5: Post-CMP    │
│   Megasonic Clean &   │
│       Metrology       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-CMP Surface Preparation & Pad Conditioning:**
   - Mount polyurethane hard polishing pads on Platens 1 and 2; mount a soft poromeric buff pad on Platen 3.
   - Perform in-situ diamond disc pad conditioning (100–120 grit) under continuous deionized (DI) water flushing to stabilize pad asperities.
   - Inspect pre-CMP blanket tungsten (CVD W) overburden thickness across 8F² shared bitline contact test fields.

2. **Platen 1: Bulk Tungsten Removal & Endpoint Detection:**
   - Dispense acidic ferric nitrate/alumina or silica-based W slurry.
   - Set platen/carrier counter-rotation with controlled down-force (2.5–3.5 psi).
   - Engage optical reflectometry or eddy-current in-situ endpoint detection (EPD) to capture the sharp slope change as the bulk W layer is cleared and the Ti/TiN barrier is reached.

3. **Platen 2: Ti/TiN Barrier Polish & Planarization:**
   - Switch to high-selectivity barrier removal slurry (W:Ti/TiN:SiO₂ selectivity tuned to suppress oxide erosion).
   - Polish until the Ti/TiN barrier over the inter-layer dielectric (ILD) oxide is fully cleared.

4. **Platen 3: Controlled Over-Polish Buff & Oxide Stop:**
   - Apply a strictly timed over-polish window (5% to 10% maximum margin) to clear residual W micro-puddles in dense array areas without inducing metal recess or dielectric erosion across the 360 nm to 400 nm bitline/wordline array pitch.
   - Perform soft pad buffing with diluted colloidal silica or alkaline surfactant chemistry to passivate plug tops.

5. **Post-CMP Cleaning & Dishing/Erosion Metrology:**
   - Transfer wafer immediately to post-CMP double-sided PVA brush scrubbing with dilute NH₄OH/citric acid, followed by megasonic DI water immersion rinse and spin dry.
   - Load wafer into High-Resolution Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) / Optical Profiler to quantify W-plug dishing and array oxide erosion around the 180 nm channel length and 220 nm width access transistor cell boundaries.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage & Polish Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2)** | $\le \pm 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Metrology Optical Alignment Station *(Source 3)* |
| **Contact / Bitline Array Pitch Uniformity** | $360\text{ to }400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Critical Dimension SEM (CD-SEM) *(Source 2)* |
| **Bitline Access Transistor Channel Critical Dimensions** | $L = 180$, $W = 220$ | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Top-down CD-SEM *(Source 1)* |
| **W-Plug Recess & Dishing Margin** | $\le 10$ | $\text{nm}$ | High-Resolution Tapping-Mode AFM |
| **Array Oxide Erosion Across 8F² Cell Field** | $\le 15$ | $\text{nm}$ | Optical Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / AFM Profilometry |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

- **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Defines the 180nm 8F² unit cell topology with access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, where bitline contacts are shared between adjacent cells and isolated via tungsten plugs (W-plugs).
- **[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Establishes bitline and wordline array pitch dimensions of $360\text{ nm to }400\text{ nm}$ and 1T1C stacked capacitor cell integration rules.
- **[Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)]**: Provides the baseline alignment and stage tolerance benchmark for Gen 2 tooling at $\pm 5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (improved from Gen 1 $\pm 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) and DI water rinsing regimes.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Sub-threshold Leakage & Contact Resistance Electrical Metrology Benchmarking

- **Document ID**: `SOP-MET-180-042`
- **Module**: Metrology / Device Characterization & Parametric Testing (PCM)
- **Hierarchy Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout ($8F^2$) > Access Transistor Diffusion & Shared Bitline Contact Layout Definition ($8F^2$)
- **Action Type**: Make
- **Technology Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm)

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Wafer Thermal Soak   │
│        at 85C         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Access Transistor   │
│   Ioff Measurement    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Shared Bitline     │
│  Contact Kelvin Test  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│       Metrology       │
│   Benchmarking and    │
│      Disposition      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Wafer Loading & Thermal Equilibrium Setup**:
   - Transfer wafer to automated parametric chuck. Set and stabilize chuck temperature to **$85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** to replicate worst-case DRAM array thermal retention and refresh degradation conditions.
   - Align probe card to PCM scribe-line test arrays targeting the isolated $8F^2$ access transistor test structures ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and shared bitline Kelvin contact pads.

2. **Access Transistor Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage Measurement ($I_{\text{off}}$)**:
   - Configure Source Measurement Unit (SMU) in high-resolution, low-current mode (fA resolution range).
   - Bias conditions:
     - Substrate/Well: $V_{\text{BB}} = -0.5\text{ V}$ to $0.0\text{ V}$ (well bias).
     - Source (Shared Bitline side): $V_{\text{S}} = 0.0\text{ V}$.
     - Gate (Wordline): $V_{\text{GS}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ (unselected state).
     - Drain (Storage Node side): $V_{\text{DS}} = V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$.
   - Perform integration sweep ($t_{\text{int}} \ge 200\text{ ms}$) to extract steady-state sub-threshold channel leakage and drain junction leakage current ($I_{\text{off}}$) per single cell at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

3. **Shared Bitline Contact Resistance Characterization ($R_{\text{cont}}$)**:
   - Contact probe pads on dedicated 4-point Kelvin and contact-chain test structures for the shared tungsten plug (W-plug) landing onto active diffusion between two adjacent access transistors.
   - Apply a forced current $I_{\text{force}} = 10\text{ }\mu\text{A}$ to $100\text{ }\mu\text{A}$ across force terminals; measure voltage drop $V_{\text{sense}}$ across sense terminals.
   - Calculate single W-plug-to-diffusion contact resistance:
     $$R_{\text{cont}} = \frac{V_{\text{sense}}}{I_{\text{force}}}$$

4. **Statistical Benchmarking & Lot Disposition**:
   - Measure 9 sites per wafer (center, inner, middle, and edge dice) across 5 sample wafers per lot.
   - Verify all measured parameters against defined PCM acceptance gates. Generate lot distribution curves (Weibull / cumulative probability) for both $I_{\text{off}}$ and $R_{\text{cont}}$.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter | Symbol | Target / Upper Limit | Measurement Unit | Test Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Access Transistor Leakage Current** | $I_{\text{off}}$ | **$\le 1.0$** | **fA/cell** | $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{\text{GS}} = 0\text{ V}$, $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ |
| **Access Transistor Channel Length** | $L$ | **$180 \pm 10$** | **nm** | CD-SEM / In-line electrical $L_{\text{eff}}$ extract |
| **Access Transistor Channel Width** | $W$ | **$220 \pm 12$** | **nm** | CD-SEM / In-line electrical $W_{\text{eff}}$ extract |
| **Shared Bitline W-Plug Contact Resistance** | $R_{\text{cont}}$ | **$\le 50.0$** | **$\Omega$/contact** | Kelvin 4-point probe, room temp ($25^\circ\text{C}$) |

---

### Literature Citations & Verification Sources

1. **"180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench"**:
   - Verified physical geometry: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; shared bitline contact between adjacent memory cells with W-plug.
   - Verified thermal leakage budget: Sub-threshold and junction leakage target $\le 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention intervals.
2. **"1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets"**:
   - Footprint and parasitic parameters: $8F^2$ folded-bitline footprint ($0.259\text{ }\mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$) with storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$) confirming baseline charge retention budgets.
3. **"Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout"**:
   - Signal development margin context: Differential signal $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$ dependent on charge retention stability prior to wordline activation.

1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets (Keeth, Baker, Johnson, Lin - DRAM Circuit Design: Fundamental and High-Speed Topics)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Kelvin & Transistor Test Structure Parametric Test Mask Design

**Task ID:** `SOP-DSN-180-KELVIN-001`  
**Level:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Classification:** Circuit Design / Layout & Physical Design / Test Mask Synthesis  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the layout design, geometric dimensioning, routing, and design-rule verification for parametric test structures placed on inline wafer scribe-line test groups (kerf / test vehicle). Specifically, it guides the physical design of 4-wire Kelvin contact resistance structures (targeting the shared bitline tungsten plug contact and diffusion regions) and dedicated nMOS 1T1C access transistors ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) to bench-test sub-threshold leakage, gate dielectric integrity, and contact resistance without parasitic interconnect loading.

---

### 2. Process Flow & Step-by-Step Procedure

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Step 1: Set Grid & Access Transistor Core (L=180nm, W=220nm)"] --> B["Step 2: Construct 4-Terminal Kelvin Structure on Shared Bitline Contact"]
    B --> C["Step 3: Lay Out Pad Cage (1xN or 2xN Array at 100µm Pitch)"]
    C --> D["Step 4: Shielding & Guard-Ring Boundary Routing"]
    D --> E["Step 5: Run DRC / LVS Verification & Mask Stream Out"]
```

#### Step 1: Set Grid Resolution & Define Transistor Core Geometries
1. Set the layout environment database unit (DBU) grid to $\le 0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ (5 nm grid snap).
2. Instantiate the isolated 1T1C nMOS access transistor channel matching the core cell layout:
   - Channel Length ($L$): Exactly **$180\text{ nm}$** ($0.18\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Channel Width ($W$): Exactly **$220\text{ nm}$** ($0.22\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Gate Dielectric Layer: Thermally grown silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) thin gate oxide ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness).
3. Instantiate reference transistor variations adjacent to the nominal device:
   - Nominal: $W/L = 220\text{ nm} / 180\text{ nm}$.
   - Channel length sweep: $L = 180\text{ nm}, 200\text{ nm}, 250\text{ nm}, 350\text{ nm}$ at fixed $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Wide device: $W = 10\,\mu\text{m}, L = 180\text{ nm}$ for bulk sub-threshold swing extraction.

#### Step 2: Construct 4-Terminal Kelvin Test Structure for Shared Bitline W-Plug
1. Define the diffusion active area (OD/RX) representing the shared node between two adjacent DRAM cells.
2. Place a single contact hole representing the bitline contact ($0.18\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$) filled with tungsten plug (W-plug).
3. Construct the 4-wire force-sense Kelvin geometry:
   - **Force Line 1 ($I^+$):** Top-level Metal 1 line routing current through the W-plug into the active diffusion.
   - **Force Line 2 ($I^-$):** Diffusion tap leading away from the contact to ground.
   - **Sense Line 1 ($V^+$):** Independent Metal 1 trace connected directly to the top edge of the contact interface without sharing current path with $I^+$.
   - **Sense Line 2 ($V^-$):** Independent diffusion branch tapped directly at the base of the contact interface without carrying current from $I^-$.
4. Ensure minimum metal-to-metal spacing complies with the bitline pitch constraint of **$360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$**.

#### Step 3: Parametric Probe Pad Routing (Standard Kerf Frame)
1. Instantiate standard wire-probe / parametric probe pad arrays ($70\,\mu\text{m} \times 70\,\mu\text{m}$ passivation openings with $100\,\mu\text{m}$ center-to-center pitch) in a 1×8 or 2×12 pad cage configuration:
   - Pad 1: Kelvin Force+ ($I_{BL}$)
   - Pad 2: Kelvin Sense+ ($V_{BL}$)
   - Pad 3: Kelvin Sense- ($V_{DIFF}$)
   - Pad 4: Kelvin Force- ($I_{DIFF}$)
   - Pad 5: Access Transistor Gate / Wordline ($V_G$)
   - Pad 6: Access Transistor Drain / BL ($V_D$)
   - Pad 7: Access Transistor Source / Storage Node ($V_S$)
   - Pad 8: P-Well / Substrate Bulk Bias ($V_B$)
2. Route interconnect traces from test structures to pads using wide Metal 1/Metal 2 buses ($\ge 2\,\mu\text{m}$) to minimize lead resistance while keeping sense traces isolated from high-current paths.

#### Step 4: Guard-Ring Enclosure and Noise Isolation
1. Enclose the sensitive sub-threshold and Kelvin test structures inside a continuous $\text{P}^+$ substrate guard ring biased to ground/bulk.
2. Maintain a minimum separation of $\ge 5\,\mu\text{m}$ between adjacent test modules to eliminate substrate carrier cross-talk during elevated temperature metrology (up to $85^\circ\text{C}$).

#### Step 5: DRC, LVS, and GDSII/OASIS Mask Export
1. Execute Design Rule Check (DRC) against 180nm CMOS ground rules (verifying contact enclosure, gate extension, active spacing, and antenna rules).
2. Execute Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) extracting parasitic resistances and confirming four isolated electrical terminals per Kelvin structure.
3. Stream out final layout data to GDSII/OASIS layer format for mask reticle assembly.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Exact Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Access Transistor Gate Length ($L$)** | $180$ | $\pm 9$ ($\pm 5\%$) | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Critical Dimension SEM (CD-SEM) |
| **Access Transistor Gate Width ($W$)** | $220$ | $\pm 11$ ($\pm 5\%$) | $\text{nm}$ | Inline CD-SEM |
| **Bitline & Wordline Contact / Interconnect Pitch** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | Min $360$, Max $400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Optical / CD-SEM Metrology |
| **Parasitic Sensing Trace Resistance** | $< 5.0$ | $\le 10.0$ | $\Omega$ | 2-Point Wire Metrology on Kelvin Sense Lines |
| **Target Parametric Leakage Floor Compatibility** | $< 1.0$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ | Maximum $1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Automated Sub-threshold $I_{off}$ Parametric Tester |

---

### 4. Verified Literature & Context Citations

1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Access transistor physical dimensions: Channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Shared bitline contact via tungsten plug (W-plug) connecting adjacent memory cells.
   - Sub-threshold and junction leakage target specification: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain retention intervals.
2. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
   - Bitline and wordline wiring pitch: approximately $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Gate oxide dielectric: thermally grown silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) with physical thickness $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ ($850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation).
3. **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
   - Parasitic capacitance and bitline loading considerations ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$, $C_s \approx 25\text{ to } 28\text{ fF}$) establishing layout requirements for Kelvin decoupling of parasitic line series resistances.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)
Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout (Keeth & Baker - DRAM Circuit Design: A Tutorial)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Sub-pA Cryo/Thermal Wafer Prober Setup & Calibration

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Chamber Purge & Dry   │
│           N2           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Thermal Conditioning  │
│          85°C          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Triaxial Guard Check  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    SMU Zero-Offset     │
│        Nulling         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Touchdown Alignment   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Leakage Metrology    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Environmental Enclosure Purge & Condensation Prevention**
   - Seal the dark shielding test enclosure around the automated wafer prober chuck.
   - Initiate continuous dry $N_2$ purge flow into the chamber until dew point drops below $-60^\circ\text{C}$ to prevent moisture condensation during thermal transitions.

2. **Thermal Chuck Conditioning & Stabilization**
   - Configure the thermal chuck controller to the target baseline qualification temperature of **$85^\circ\text{C}$** (or required cryo-temperature profile).
   - Allow thermal soak for at least 15 minutes until temperature variation across the chuck surface settles within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

3. **Sub-pA Triaxial Guarding & Cabling Verification**
   - Connect high-isolation triaxial cabling from the Source Measure Unit (SMU) pre-amplifiers to the prober probe arm manipulators.
   - Verify driven active guard rings and shielding continuity to minimize stray cable capacitance and leakage path resistance ($R_{\text{iso}} > 100\,\text{T}\Omega$).

4. **Open/Short SMU Zero-Offset Nulling & System Calibration**
   - Lift probes to the open-circuit reference position ($Z = +500\,\mu\text{m}$ above wafer surface).
   - Execute internal SMU hardware auto-zero, cable capacitance compensation, and sub-femtoamp current offset cancellation across integration apertures (PLC $\ge 5$).

5. **Automated Vision Pattern Recognition & Touchdown Alignment**
   - Load the 180nm DRAM test vehicle wafer onto the vacuum chuck.
   - Run optical pattern recognition on dedicated alignment fiducials to compensate for wafer theta ($\theta$) skew.
   - Align tungsten/beryllium-copper probe needles over the test structure pads (targeting shared bitline contacts and diffusion test structures for $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$ access transistors).
   - Execute calibrated Z-touchdown with controlled overdrive ($35 \pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$) to establish stable ohmic contact without puncturing the underlying barrier or landing pads.

6. **Sub-Threshold Leakage & Contact Resistance Measurement**
   - Execute parametric sweeps measuring sub-threshold off-state leakage ($I_{\text{off}}$) and contact resistance.
   - Verify that background system noise floor does not obscure target femtoamp evaluation.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Leakage Current Noise Floor** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA}$ (femtoampere) | Open-circuit chuck state at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with driven guard |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature** | $85.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Thermally stabilized chuck surface under dry $\text{N}_2$ ambient |
| **Transistor Sub-threshold Leakage** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Measured across $L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$ access transistor at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Cell Capacitance Parametric Budget** | $25.0 \text{ to } 30.0$ | $\text{fF}$ (femtofarad) | Stacked storage node test capacitor (minimum specification $\ge 25\,\text{fF}$) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - *Context applied*: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, channel width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$; leakage current target must be kept below **$1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$** to maintain required refresh characteristics; minimum capacitance budget of $\ge 28\,\text{fF}$ per cell.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - *Context applied*: 1T1C stacked capacitor target of **$25\text{ to }30\,\text{fF}$** per cell ensures data retention $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at **$85^\circ\text{C}$**; bitline/wordline pitch at $360\text{ to }400\,\text{nm}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
  - *Context applied*: Access transistor charge dump dynamics with nominal cell storage capacitance $C_s \approx 25\,\text{fF}$ against bitline capacitance $C_{BL} \approx 250\,\text{fF}$, validating the need for sub-pA/sub-fA instrumentation sensitivity during metrology benchmarking.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)
Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout (Keeth & Baker - DRAM Circuit Design: A Tutorial)

nodes.primary_metric: Engineering Tolerance as per Gen 2 (µm)
nodes.sop_content:
```text
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               DRAM FOUNDATION VN -- ELECTRICAL METROLOGY & PARAMETRIC TEST                         |
|      85°C Sub-threshold Leakage & Kelvin Contact Resistance Parametric Extraction                  |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 1. Document Control & Objective
- **Module Path:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` > `1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²)` > `Metrology` > `85°C Sub-threshold Leakage & Kelvin Contact Resistance Parametric Extraction`
- **Objective:** Quantify sub-threshold leakage ($I_{\text{sub}}$) at high-temperature operating conditions ($85^\circ\text{C}$) on access transistors ($W/L = 220\,\text{nm} / 180\,\text{nm}$) and verify shared bitline contact interface resistance ($R_c$) via 4-terminal Kelvin bridge test structures to validate retention time $>64\,\text{ms}$.

---

### 2. Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

#### Step 1: Thermal Chuck Conditioning & Environmental Stabilization
1. Mount the 180nm production/test wafer onto the automated wafer prober thermal chuck.
2. Set the thermal chuck temperature controller to **$85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.
3. Seal the prober enclosure and purge with dry nitrogen ($N_2$) to prevent moisture condensation and thermal drift. Allow thermal equilibrium stabilization for $\ge 15\,\text{minutes}$.

#### Step 2: Prober Alignment & Kelvin Needle Contact Verification
1. Optically align the probe card needles to the 4-terminal Kelvin contact test structures and adjacent $8\text{F}^2$ access transistor test macros.
2. Execute controlled probe overdrive ($35\,\mu\text{m}$ to $50\,\mu\text{m}$) onto the aluminum/tungsten probe pads.
3. Perform open/short contact checks across force/sense terminals; verify probe-to-pad contact resistance $< 1.5\,\Omega$ prior to test initiation.

#### Step 3: 4-Terminal Kelvin Bitline Contact Resistance Extraction
1. Connect Source Monitor Unit (SMU 1) to the force pad of the shared bitline contact (W-plug to access transistor diffusion node) and SMU 2 to the sense pad.
2. Apply a constant DC force current $I_{\text{force}} = 100\,\mu\text{A}$ across the force lines and measure differential voltage drop $V_{\text{sense}}$ across the Kelvin sense lines.
3. Compute the specific Kelvin contact resistance:
   $$R_c = \frac{V_{\text{sense}}}{I_{\text{force}}}$$
4. Repeat measurement across 5 site locations (Center, North, South, East, West) per wafer to evaluate tungsten plug contact interface uniformity.

#### Step 4: 85°C Sub-threshold Leakage ($I_{\text{sub}}$) & $I_{\text{off}}$ Parametric Extraction
1. Configure triaxial SMUs on the access transistor test module ($W = 220\,\text{nm}$, $L = 180\,\text{nm}$):
   - Drain (BL terminal): Force $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
   - Source (Storage node contact): Grounded ($0.0\,\text{V}$).
   - Substrate/Well: Grounded or back-bias condition ($V_{\text{BB}} = 0.0\,\text{V}$ / $-0.5\,\text{V}$).
2. Sweep gate voltage (WL terminal) from $V_{\text{GS}} = -0.5\,\text{V}$ to $+1.8\,\text{V}$ with triaxial low-current resolution ($0.1\,\text{fA}$ floor, $100\,\text{ms}$ integration aperture).
3. Measure and record off-state drain leakage at $V_{\text{GS}} = 0\,\text{V}$ ($I_{\text{off}}$) at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
4. Calculate sub-threshold swing ($S$) and confirm the off-state leakage meets cell refresh retention requirements.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Extraction Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Chuck Temperature Setpoint & Stability** | **$85.0 \pm 0.5$** | **$^\circ\text{C}$** | Steady-state thermal equilibrium during probing |
| **Access Transistor Leakage Current ($I_{\text{off}}$)** | **$< 1.0$** | **$\text{fA/cell}$** | Measured at $85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{\text{GS}} = 0.0\,\text{V}$, $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ ($W/L = 220/180\,\text{nm}$) |
| **Kelvin Shared Bitline Contact Resistance ($R_c$)** | **$< 45.0$** | **$\Omega/\text{contact}$** | 4-point Kelvin Kelvin extraction at $I_{\text{force}} = 100\,\mu\text{A}$ on W-plug contact |
| **Cell Retention Assurance Threshold** | **$> 64$** | **$\text{ms}$** | Derived refresh interval budget at $85^\circ\text{C}$ under $C_s \ge 25\,\text{fF}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations
1. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
   - Access transistor geometry: Channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - Shared bitline contact layout between adjacent cells connected via tungsten plug (W-plug).
   - Off-state leakage target: *"Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval"*.
2. **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**:
   - Data retention requirement: *"maintain a minimum capacitance of 25 to 30 fF (femtofarads) per cell to ensure data retention time > 64 ms at 85°C"*.
   - Structural geometry: $8\text{F}^2$ cell footprint with bitline and wordline pitch around $360\,\text{nm}$ to $400\,\text{nm}$.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)
Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout (Keeth & Baker - DRAM Circuit Design: A Tutorial)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Quality Acceptance & Metrology Protocol for Access Transistor Diffusion & Shared Bitline Contact Layout Definition ($8F^2$)

- **Document ID:** `SOP-QA-180NM-DRAM-8F2-DIFF-BC-001`
- **Revision:** 1.0
- **Process Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)
- **Classification:** Quality Assurance & Metrology Standard

---

### 1. Metrology & Acceptance Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Step 1: CD-SEM     │
│       Inspection       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Step 2: Overlay &    │
│       Alignment        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 3: Contact     │
│     Profile & Etch     │
│       Metrology        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Step 4: Junction    │
│  Leakage & Electrical  │
│           QA           │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Step 1: CD-SEM Critical Dimension Metrology**
   - Load wafer into automated CD-SEM tool (e.g., in-line top-down SEM).
   - Measure active diffusion area width across 9 test sites per die: verify target channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ and gate channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$.
   - Measure shared bitline contact (BC) critical dimension and wordline/bitline pitch targets ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$).

2. **Step 2: Overlay & Lithography Alignment Verification**
   - Measure overlay error between active diffusion (OD) and shared bitline contact mask layers using optical/scatterometry overlay metrology targets.
   - Verify symmetric placement of the shared contact between adjacent memory cells to prevent asymmetric contact resistance or junction breakdown.

3. **Step 3: Dielectric Etch Profile & Gate Oxide Integrity Inspection**
   - Conduct cross-sectional inline scatterometry/ellipsometry to inspect thermally grown gate dielectric thickness (target $3.5\text{ nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$ grown via $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation).
   - Verify contact etch profile into shared diffusion node for complete oxide punch-through without excessive silicon gouging/recess.

4. **Step 4: Electrical Junction Leakage & Parametric Screening**
   - Route wafer to automated parametric test station (PCM / e-test).
   - Heat wafer chuck to thermal stress limit ($85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Bias shared bitline contact node and measure access transistor sub-threshold and reverse-biased junction leakage current across cell arrays.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
               Target Physical Specifications (180nm 8F²)               
           ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   
    L (nm) │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 180                    │   
    W (nm) │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ 220             │   
Pitch (nm) │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ 360-400 │   
T_ox (nm)  │█ 3.5                                                   │   
           └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   
                                                                        
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Allowed Tolerance / Limit | Test Method / Machine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Access Transistor Channel Geometry** | $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 10\%\ (\pm 18\text{ nm} \text{ on } L, \pm 22\text{ nm} \text{ on } W)$ | In-line CD-SEM (Automated Wafer Metrology) |
| **Wordline / Bitline Pitch** | $360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$ | Within $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ specification window | CD-SEM / Diffraction Scatterometry |
| **Gate Dielectric Physical Thickness** | $3.5\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 0.3\text{ nm}$ (thermally grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / TEM Reference |
| **Junction & Sub-threshold Leakage** | $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ | Max $\le 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (to guarantee $>64\text{ ms}$ retention) | Parametric Electrical Wafer Prober (PCM) |

---

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: Length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, Width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Shared bitline contact architecture between two adjacent memory cells.
  - Sub-threshold and junction leakage limit: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - $8F^2$ cell layout architecture with bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
  - Gate dielectric physical thickness: $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$ thermally grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation.
  - Retention requirement: $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

nodes.primary_metric: Sub-milestone of Quality Acceptance & Metrology Protocol for Access Transistor Diffusion & Shared Bitline Contact Layout Definition (8F²)
nodes.sop_content:
```text
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| DRAM FOUNDATION VN - METROLOGY & PROCESS INTEGRATION DIVISION                                      |
| STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP): SOP-MET-180-042                                                |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| TITLE: Define CD-SEM & Overlay Metrology Target Layout for Diffusion & Shared BL Contact           |
| NODE: 180nm Planar DRAM (Gen 2: µm Scale) | CELL TOPOLOGY: 8F² Folded Bitline (0.259 µm²)          |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 1. Process Objective & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure establishes the physical design, layout integration, and automated measurement recipes for:
1. **CD-SEM Metrology Targets** measuring active area (OD/Diffusion) critical dimension ($W = 220\text{ nm}$, gate length nominal $L = 180\text{ nm}$) and shared Bitline Contact (BLC) plug CD ($180\text{ nm}$).
2. **Optical & Scanning Electron Overlay Targets** (Box-in-Box / Bar-in-Bar / AIM targets) verifying alignment between the shared tungsten bitline contact (W-plug) layer and the underlying active silicon diffusion active area.
3. Test coupon placement in the scribe line / kerf channels (100 µm width) and array edge regions.

---

### 2. Physical Layout Architecture & Target Specifications

```
                       Diffusion (OD) & Shared BLC Layout
     |<------------------------ 8F² Cell Pitch ------------------------->|
     +-------------------------------------------------------------------+
     |                      Active Diffusion (OD)                        |
     |   [ Storage Node ]       [ Gate/WL ]   ( Shared BLC )  [ Gate/WL ]|
     |      Contact Pad           L=180nm       Dia = 180nm     L=180nm  |
     |         (SN)                            (W-Plug)                  |
     |                                                                   |
     |   +---------------+      +---------+    +---------+   +---------+ | ---
     |   |   Node Diff   |======| Channel |====| BL Diff |===| Channel | |  | W = 220 nm
     |   +---------------+      +---------+    +---------+   +---------+ | ---
     +-------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: CD-SEM In-Die & Kerf Target Definition
1. **Active Diffusion (OD) Target Layout:**
   - Define isolated and dense 1D/2D lines in the kerf: Line width $W = 0.220\text{ µm}$ ($220\text{ nm}$), pitch $P = 0.440\text{ µm}$ for array-representative dense patterns.
   - Channel length calibration line: Pitch $L = 0.180\text{ µm}$ ($180\text{ nm}$) gate slot simulation over continuous active area.
2. **Shared Bitline Contact (BLC) Target Layout:**
   - Target opening: Square contact hole of nominal design dimension $0.180\text{ µm} \times 0.180\text{ µm}$ (aspect ratio $\approx 2.5:1$ to $3:1$ through pre-metal dielectric).
   - Kerf Array Test Matrix: $5 \times 5$ contact hole matrix placed on pitch matching active transistor drain landing pad ($0.360\text{ µm}$ pitch).
3. **TLM Structure Integration:**
   - Place transmission line measurement pads adjacent to kerf targets ($W = 100\text{ µm}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\text{ µm}$) with staggered pad spacings $d \in \{5, 10, 20, 40, 80\}\text{ µm}$ to monitor specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c$) and active diffusion sheet resistance ($R_s$).

#### Step 2: Overlay Metrology Target Layout (BLC-to-Diffusion)
1. **Target Architecture (Box-in-Box / Frame-in-Frame):**
   - **Outer Frame (Layer 1 - Active Diffusion / OD):** $20\text{ µm} \times 20\text{ µm}$ outer boundary, trench width $2.0\text{ µm}$, etched into zero-layer/active silicon.
   - **Inner Box (Layer 2 - Shared Bitline Contact / W-Plug):** $10\text{ µm} \times 10\text{ µm}$ inner square array centered concentrically within the outer frame.
2. **Micro-Overlay Targets (In-Array / Array Edge):**
   - Grating-based Advanced Imaging Metrology (AIM) targets ($15\text{ µm} \times 15\text{ µm}$) placed at the 4 corners of the $8F^2$ array tile block (array unit area $= 0.259\text{ µm}^2$).

#### Step 3: CD-SEM & Overlay Automated Recipe Programming
1. **Beam Conditions:**
   - Accelerating Voltage ($V_{\text{acc}}$): $500\text{ V} - 800\text{ V}$ to prevent gate oxide charging and resist shrinkage during post-etch inspection.
   - Probe Current ($I_p$): $8\text{ pA} - 12\text{ pA}$.
2. **Measurement Algorithm:**
   - Edge threshold detection: 50% threshold on secondary electron (SE) intensity waveform.
   - Contact hole circularity & area extraction: Fit minimum enclosing ellipse; compute major axis, minor axis, and average diameter ($D_{\text{avg}}$).
3. **Overlay Algorithm:**
   - Optical / SEM centroid calculation:
     $$\Delta X = X_{\text{BLC\_Centroid}} - X_{\text{Diff\_Centroid}}, \quad \Delta Y = Y_{\text{BLC\_Centroid}} - Y_{\text{Diff\_Centroid}}$$
   - Total Overlay Vector Error: $\Delta R = \sqrt{\Delta X^2 + \Delta Y^2}$.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Metric ID | Parameter Description | Nominal Target | Tolerance / Specification Limit | Unit | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MAC-01** | Active Diffusion Line Width ($W$) | $220$ | $\pm 18$ ($202 - 238$) | $\text{nm}$ | Inline CD-SEM ($50\%$ threshold) |
| **MAC-02** | Shared Bitline Contact Hole CD (Post-Etch) | $180$ | $\pm 15$ ($165 - 195$) | $\text{nm}$ | Inline Top-down CD-SEM |
| **MAC-03** | Shared BLC to Active Diffusion Overlay ($\Delta R$) | $0.0$ | $\le 25.0$ ($3\sigma \le 30.0$) | $\text{nm}$ | Automated Optical/SEM Overlay Tool |
| **MAC-04** | $8F^2$ Folded Bitline Unit Cell Footprint | $0.259$ | $\pm 0.015$ | $\mu\text{m}^2$ | Automated Layout DRC / SEM Verification |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & References
1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - Access transistor geometry: Channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Shared bitline contact implementation between adjacent 1T1C memory cells with tungsten plug (W-plug) interconnect.
2. **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**
   - $8F^2$ folded bitline cell area footprint $= 0.259\text{ µm}^2$ at feature size $F = 180\text{ nm}$.
3. **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity**
   - Test coupon geometry: $W = 100\text{ µm}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\text{ µm}$ across pad spacings $d \in \{5, 10, 20, 40, 80\}\text{ µm}$ for measuring interface contact resistivity ($\rho_c$) and diffusion sheet resistance ($R_s$).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-180-CDSEM-001
**Title:** Design CD-SEM In-Die Feature Grating & Calibration Gauge Targets for Active Area and Bitline Contacts  
**Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 2, $\mu$m scale)  
**Cell Topology:** $8F^2$ Folded Bitline Stacked Capacitor over Bitline (COB)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Step 1: Active Area  │
│   Calibration Gauge   │
│     Target Layout     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 2: Bitline    │
│     Contact Pitch     │
│    Grating Design     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 3: In-Die     │
│   CD-SEM Metrology    │
│   Anchor Placement    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Step 4: Quality    │
│  Acceptance & Defect  │
│     Verification      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Step 1: Layout Active Area (AA) Calibration Gauge Targets**
   - In the metrology test-key frame and in-die kerf margins, instantiate 1D line/space calibration bar targets representing the access transistor active channel geometry.
   - Define nominal isolated and dense line gauge targets with critical dimension (CD) channel length target $L = 180\text{ nm}$ ($0.18\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) and active diffusion width target $W = 220\text{ nm}$ ($0.22\text{ }\mu\text{m}$).
   - Include programmed bias pitch steps ($\pm 5\text{ nm}$, $\pm 10\text{ nm}$) surrounding the nominal target to calibrate SEM beam scan non-linearity and edge roughness detection.

2. **Step 2: Layout Bitline Contact (BC) Feature Gratings**
   - Construct 2D array grating structures mimicking the shared bitline contact matrix between adjacent $8F^2$ memory cells.
   - Implement bitline and wordline pitch grating arrays across the certified pitch span of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.
   - Ensure contact gauge patterns feature symmetric surrounding dummy contacts to maintain optical proximity correction (OPC) fidelity and uniform electron beam charging dissipation during inspection.

3. **Step 3: Position In-Die Anchors & Scan Boxes for Automated SEM Navigation**
   - Define coarse-to-fine recognition optical and SEM alignment marks at the perimeter of the active cell array.
   - Set up automated SEM inspection field of view (FOV) scan windows:
     - FOV 1 (Grating pitch calibration): $2.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 2.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ across minimum 5 consecutive grating bars ($360\text{ nm}$–$400\text{ nm}$ pitch).
     - FOV 2 (Single feature measurement): $0.5\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 0.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ focused on nominal contact aperture and gate/diffusion intersection ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

4. **Step 4: Run Metrology DRC Verification & Data Integrity Export**
   - Execute DRC/LVS rules specifically on the metrology layer to ensure non-violation of minimum spacing and exclusion zones relative to operational 1T1C storage node pads.
   - Stream GDSII/OASIS patterns to the CD-SEM automated recipe generator with designated coordinates for beam landing energy and measurement thresholds.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Access Transistor Channel Length ($L$) Gauge Target** | $180 \pm 9$ | $\text{nm}$ | Top-down automated CD-SEM profile extraction |
| **Active Diffusion Channel Width ($W$) Gauge Target** | $220 \pm 11$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated CD-SEM orthogonal scan |
| **Bitline & Wordline Grating Array Pitch** | $360 \text{ to } 400$ | $\text{nm}$ | Multi-pitch diffraction & CD-SEM edge-to-edge averaging |
| **Operating Cell Junction Leakage Budget Criterion** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell (at } 85^\circ\text{C)}$ | Parametric electrical test system (pA-meter) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *“Unit Cell Geometry: Access transistor channel length L = 180 nm, width W = 220 nm. Bitline contact shared between two adjacent memory cells.”*
  - *“Leakage Current Target: Sub-threshold and junction leakage must be kept below 1 fA/cell at 85°C to achieve refresh interval...”*
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *“A classic 180nm DRAM cell uses a 1-Transistor 1-Capacitor (1T1C) architecture with an 8F^2 or 6F^2 cell layout.”*
  - *“Bitline and wordline pitch is approximately 360 nm to 400 nm.”*

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-180-OVM01
**Title:** Layout Dedicated Box-in-Box and Frame-in-Frame Overlay Metrology Marks for Diffusion-to-Contact Alignment  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Classification:** Metrology / Lithography Alignment  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the layout generation and placement protocol for optical Box-in-Box (BiB) and Frame-in-Frame (FiF) overlay metrology marks. These marks verify lithographic registration and overlay alignment error between active area diffusion (OD/FOX defining access transistor channels $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and shared tungsten-plug bitline contacts (CONT/W-plug) in an $8F^2$ folded-bitline DRAM cell architecture.

---

### 2. Required Context & Verified References
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Bitline contact is shared between two adjacent memory cells.
  - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) contacted via tungsten plug (W-plug).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - 1T1C architecture with $8F^2$ layout.
  - Bitline and wordline pitch is approximately $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 1: Define Scribe-Line Keepout & Metrology Cell Allocations                   |
| - Allocate dedicated 40 µm x 40 µm optical inspection cells in dicing streets.     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 2: Generate Outer Frame / Outer Box on Active Diffusion Layer (OD)          |
| - Draw outer square frame: 30.0 µm x 30.0 µm outer boundary, 2.0 µm linewidth.    |
| - Segment solid edges into 360-400 nm pitch sub-features to match cell density.   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 3: Generate Inner Box / Inner Frame on Shared Contact Layer (CONT)          |
| - Center inner solid square (12.0 µm x 12.0 µm) or frame (15.0 µm, 1.5 µm width)   |
|   concentric with outer diffusion mark. Target nominal clearance: 7.5 µm.        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                          |
                                          v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| STEP 4: Run DRC / DFM Symmetry and Rule Verification                             |
| - Validate 4-fold geometric symmetry (D4) and 400 nm pitch segmentation rules.    |
| - Ensure no metal CMP fill or capacitor layers overlap the mark region.           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Define Scribe-Line Keepout & Mark Allocation
1. In the layout editor (GDSII/OASIS), locate the primary scribe-line / dicing street channels adjacent to the $8F^2$ memory core arrays.
2. Instantiate a dedicated metrology cell frame of $40.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 40.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ clear window free from dummy fill, planarization tiling, or CMP dummy features.

#### Step 2: Draw Outer Diffusion Mark (Reference Layer - OD)
1. On the active diffusion mask layer (`DIFF` / `OD`), instantiate the outer metrology target:
   - **Outer Frame Outer Dimension:** $30.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 30.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.
   - **Outer Frame Line Width:** $2.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (inner perimeter boundary at $26.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 26.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$).
2. To avoid chemical-mechanical planarization (CMP) dishing and proximity-effect distortion, segment solid lines into periodic grating arrays matching the local array design rules:
   - Segmentation pitch: $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$ line/space grating along the X and Y arms.

#### Step 3: Draw Inner Contact Mark (Current Layer - CONT)
1. On the bitline contact layer (`CONT` / `W-plug`), construct the inner mark concentric to the outer diffusion frame center $(X_0, Y_0)$:
   - **Inner Box Option (BiB):** Solid square of $12.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 12.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.
   - **Inner Frame Option (FiF):** Outer edge $15.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 15.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$, line width $1.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (inner clearance $12.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 12.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$).
2. Ensure nominal design gap between inner mark perimeter and outer frame inner edge is $\ge 5.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ (nominal gap: $7.0\text{ }\mu\text{m} - 7.5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) to eliminate optical crosstalk in brightfield overlay measurement tools.

#### Step 4: Verification and Design Rule Check (DRC)
1. Verify 4-fold rotational symmetry ($D_4$ symmetry) across the horizontal and vertical axes to guarantee zero design-induced Tool-Induced Shift (TIS).
2. Execute hierarchical DRC to verify mark compliance against 180nm design rules:
   - Access transistor diffusion width ($W = 220\text{ nm}$) and gate channel clearance ($L = 180\text{ nm}$) rules do not flag false violations within the scribe-line metrology cell.
   - Contact enclosure by diffusion margin verification.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Tolerance / Bounds | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mark Pitch Segmentation** | $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ | $\pm 10\text{ nm}$ | Automated CD-SEM / Layout DRC Engine |
| **Design Center Concentricity Offset ($\Delta X, \Delta Y$)** | $0.0\text{ nm}$ (Nominal layout) | $\le 0.5\text{ nm}$ (Grid snapping error) | CAD Layout Verification / DRC |
| **Active Diffusion Channel Rule Conformity ($L / W$)** | $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ | Exact match to active rule set | GDS DRC Clean Assertion |
| **Post-Litho Overlay Error Budget ($\|\Delta_{\text{OD-CONT}}\|\le 3\sigma$)** | $< 35.0\text{ nm}$ | Upper Specification Limit (USL): $40.0\text{ nm}$ | High-Precision Optical Overlay Metrology Tool |

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title
**Generate Automated Metrology Recipe Coordinates and Optical Rule Check Verification for Scribe-Line Targets**

**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (8F² Folded Bitline Stacked Capacitor / COB Architecture)  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm / 180nm node)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Architecture

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  GDSII/OASIS Layout (Active Diffusion, Shared BL Contact, Scribe-Line Frame)          |
+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Optical Rule Check (ORC) Verification (180nm Gate L, 220nm Active W, 1.3 µm PR)      |
+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Scribe-Line Target Coordinate Extraction (CD-SEM & Optical Film Profiling)           |
+------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Automated Metrology Recipe Compilation (9-pt / 49-pt Radial Wafer Map Formats)       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Layout Layer & Scribe-Line Target Ingestion**
   - Import the final GDSII/OASIS stream containing the active diffusion mask (OD), bitline contact mask (CB), and dedicated scribe-line metrology frame.
   - Filter and parse target structures:
     - Critical Dimension (CD) line/space test gratings for access transistor active diffusion ($W = 220\text{ nm}$) and channel gate length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$).
     - Scribe-line optical test pads dedicated to dielectric stacks and photoresist film monitoring ($1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ nominal thickness).
     - Box-in-box / frame-in-frame overlay marks between the shared bitline contact (CB) and the underlying active diffusion region.

2. **Optical Rule Check (ORC) & Proximity Verification**
   - Run design rule and optical rule checks across all scribe-line metrology targets to detect optical proximity distortion and marginal pattern resolution.
   - Verify pattern fidelity using calibrated optical models ($\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$) for film reflections and verify that non-clearing or bridging conditions do not exist in test pitches.
   - Ensure an optical clearance exclusion buffer surrounds every scribe-line test target to prevent optical diffraction flare from neighboring dummy fill structures.

3. **Coordinate Extraction & Anchor Alignment Registration**
   - Extract primary die-pitch step-and-repeat offsets and absolute $(X, Y)$ coordinate vectors for global alignment marks and local targets relative to the wafer center $(0,0)$.
   - Generate dual-tier navigational coordinates:
     - **Low-magnification optical pre-alignment coordinates** (field of view $> 150\ \mu\text{m}$).
     - **High-magnification CD-SEM / Ellipsometry stage coordinates** targeted at the centroid of the measurement grating.

4. **Metrology Recipe Generation & Wafer Map Sequencing**
   - Format stage drive vectors into tool-specific recipe files:
     - Program automated 9-point or 49-point radial wafer inspection maps for optical film profiling and critical dimension uniformity tracking across spin coating and furnace runs.
     - Embed auto-focus, auto-stigmator, and beam current/acceleration voltage calibration routines at the first global anchor site.

5. **Recipe Validation & Dry-Run Verification**
   - Perform software dry-run simulation of the generated recipe against the physical stage travel limits and collision envelopes.
   - Verify recipe coordinate syntax, target autofocus contrast score thresholds, and handoff to the fab automated execution system.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transistor Diffusion Critical Dimension (W)** | $220.0 \pm 11.0$ | $\text{nm}$ (at 180nm node) | CD-SEM automated measurement |
| **Transistor Gate Channel Length (L)** | $180.0 \pm 9.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | CD-SEM automated measurement |
| **Photoresist Film Target Thickness (PR)** | $1300 \pm 2$ | $\text{nm}$ ($\mu\text{m}$ film control) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |
| **Wafer Metrology Map Sampling Density** | Automated 9-point or 49-point radial map | discrete points / wafer | Recipe sequence verification |

---

### 4. Literature Context & Source Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Applied access transistor unit cell dimensions: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ for critical dimension target extraction and shared bitline contact integration.
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**
  - Applied optical modeling equation ($\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$), photoresist target thickness of $1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ monitored with $\pm 2\text{ nm}$ precision, and the standardized automated 9-point or 49-point radial wafer mapping grid for film uniformity tracking.

```text
│                        │
│   Pitch & Tolerance    │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Mount & Inspect Calibration Reticle**:
   - Secure the standard calibration target onto the optical projection aligner stage.
   - Inspect the reticle surface under magnification (10x Plan Achromat objective, NA 0.25) to ensure optical elements and chrome calibration gratings are free from particulate contamination.
2. **Align Optical Axes & Illumination**:
   - Engage the 365nm i-line UV source (high-power UV LED / mercury lamp).
   - Set stage z-focus across standard pitch test patterns representing access transistor active areas and shared bitline contacts.
3. **Execute Optical Proximity & Linewidth Metrology Routine**:
   - Align the reticle to stage reference fiducials, locking in positional registration within Gen 2 mechanical travel limits.
   - Perform optical contrast and edge-detection scans across test gratings matching the bitline/wordline layout pitch.
   - Verify critical dimensional fidelity representing the access transistor gate length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$) and channel width ($W = 220\text{ nm}$) scaled across the projection optics.
4. **Calibrate Recipe & Log Recipe Parameters**:
   - Save the calibrated magnification, illumination intensity, and focus offsets into the metrology recipe profile for 180nm 8F² cell inspection.

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Cell Geometry: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ in 8F² folded bitline architecture.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Execute In-Line SEM Inspection & Contact Resistance Acceptance Verification

- **Module**: Quality Assurance & Metrology / 180nm Open-Source DRAM (8F² Folded Bitline Architecture)
- **Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > 1T1C DRAM Cell Topology & Layout (8F²) > Quality Acceptance & Metrology Protocol > Execute In-Line SEM Inspection & Contact Resistance Acceptance Verification
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm
- **Action Type**: Make / Verification

---

## 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Wafer Loading &    │
│       Alignment       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  CD-SEM Inspection:   │
│    Gate L & Diff W    │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    CD-SEM: Bitline    │
│    Contact Hole &     │
│        Overlay        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Four-Point Probe    │
│   Kelvin Sensing on   │
│       TLM Array       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Extract Rc, Rs &    │
│  Transfer Length LT   │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Disposition: Pass /  │
│   Quarantine Wafer    │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Automated Wafer Loading & Die Alignment
1. Load 200mm / 8-inch production wafer onto the automated metrology chuck.
2. Initialize global optical alignment to array fiducial marks, orienting the array along the 8F² folded bitline coordinate axes.
3. Establish vacuum lock (< $10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$) and beam current conditions for low-voltage in-line Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscopy (CD-SEM) to minimize charging on unpassivated dielectric surfaces.

### Step 2: In-Line CD-SEM Array Critical Dimension Inspection
1. Navigate CD-SEM to the access transistor active area test sites (minimum 9 dies per wafer: center, edge-exclusion zones, and 4 orthogonal quadrants).
2. Measure the physical access transistor channel length: target nominal **$L = 180\text{ nm}$**.
3. Measure the access transistor diffusion active width: target nominal **$W = 220\text{ nm}$**.
4. Inspect the shared bitline contact opening post-etch / pre-metallization at the boundary of adjacent memory cells to verify complete oxide clearance without substrate pitting.

### Step 3: TLM Structure Kelvin Four-Point Measurement
1. Steer the automated parametric probe card to the in-die Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) test keys.
2. Verify TLM test structure dimensions:
   - Contact pad width: **$W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$**
   - Contact pad length: **$L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$**
   - Progressive inter-pad spacings: **$d \in \{5\ \mu\text{m}, 10\ \mu\text{m}, 20\ \mu\text{m}, 40\ \mu\text{m}, 80\ \mu\text{m}\}$**
3. Perform four-point Kelvin current-force / voltage-sense measurements between each adjacent pad pair:
   - Force low-level constant DC current $I_{\text{test}}$ to avoid local Joule heating.
   - Sense differential voltage drop $V_{\text{sense}}$ across pad pairs separated by spacing $d$.
   - Record total resistance:
     $$R_T = \frac{V_{\text{sense}}}{I_{\text{test}}}$$

### Step 4: Regression Extraction of $R_c$, $R_s$, and Specific Contact Resistivity ($\rho_c$)
1. Fit measured resistance data to the TLM linear formulation:
   $$R_T = 2 R_c + \left(\frac{R_s}{W}\right) d$$
2. Extract parameters from linear regression:
   - **Diffusion Sheet Resistance ($R_s$)**: Calculated directly from the slope $m = R_s / W \implies R_s = m \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - **Contact Resistance ($R_c$)**: Extracted from the y-intercept at $d = 0$: $Y_0 = 2 R_c \implies R_c = Y_0 / 2$.
   - **Transfer Length ($L_T$)**: Extracted from the negative x-intercept: $X_0 = -2 L_T \implies L_T = -X_0 / 2$.
   - **Specific Contact Resistivity ($\rho_c$)**: Compute $\rho_c = R_c \times W \times L_T = R_s \times L_T^2\ [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$.

---

## 3. Dimensional Reference Summary

```text
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░                              │
TLM Pad L (um)┤░░░░░░░░░░                              │
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                     │
TLM Pad W (um)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                     │
 Access W (nm)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
 Access L (nm)┤█████████████████████████████████       │
              │█████████████████████████████████       │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0        55        110      165      220 
```

---

## 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Metric # | Inspection / Verification Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Metrology Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-1** | Access Transistor Gate Length ($L$) | $180 \pm 10$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-Line CD-SEM Top-Down Inspection |
| **AC-2** | Access Transistor Diffusion Width ($W$) | $220 \pm 12$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-Line CD-SEM Top-Down Inspection |
| **AC-3** | Unit Cell Footprint Area (8F² Folded Bitline) | $0.259$ | $\mu\text{m}^2$ | CD-SEM 2D Spatial Area Mapping ($F = 180\text{ nm}$) |
| **AC-4** | TLM Contact Test Structure Geometry | $W = 100$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50$, $d = [5, 10, 20, 40, 80]$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Automated Optical / CD Metrology & Kelvin Probe Station |

---

## 5. Source Citations & References

- **Source 1**: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*  
  - Verified values: 180nm generation 8F² folded bitline cell; Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; Shared bitline contact between adjacent memory cells; Tungsten plug (W-plug).
- **Source 2**: *1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets*  
  - Verified values: Folded bitline 8F² footprint cell area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at feature size $F = 180\text{ nm}$ ($0.194\ \mu\text{m}^2$ for 6F² open bitline).
- **Source 3**: *Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity*  
  - Verified values: Pad geometry $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$; spacing increments $d = 5\ \mu\text{m}, 10\ \mu\text{m}, 20\ \mu\text{m}, 40\ \mu\text{m}, 80\ \mu\text{m}$; analytical extraction equations $R_T = 2R_c + (R_s / W)d$ and $\rho_c = R_c \cdot W \cdot L_T = R_s \cdot L_T^2\ [\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^2]$.
